question: Does language-centroid removal suppress real multilingual encoder language leakage while preserving intent signal, and does it do so more specifically than generic controls?
claim_boundary: Real frozen-encoder representation diagnostic only. No linguistic-relativity, cognition, translation-quality, universal-representation, or fine-tuned-model claim.

dataset.selection: For each locale and intent, rank examples by SHA-256(seed || id); select the first 20 fit examples and first 20 evaluation examples. Fail closed if any locale-intent cell has fewer than 20 examples in either split.

primary_probe: nearest-centroid Euclidean classifier fit only on the fit split

transforms.language_centering: subtract each locale's fit-split embedding centroid from fit and evaluation embeddings of that locale
transforms.random_group_centering: assign records to 3 deterministic SHA-256 groups per seed and subtract fit centroids for those pseudo-groups
transforms.random_subspace: remove projection onto 2 deterministic Gaussian orthonormal directions per seed

failure_evidence.failure: Cell ('en-US', 'audio_volume_other') has 18 train rows; v1 required 20.

authorization_scope: Archived failed feasibility protocol. Never rerun as the active protocol.
